title: HSE Engineer
description: Company Description Dorsch Global is a worldwide network of planning and consulting companies that transforms complex challenges into practical solutions. With about 7,500 employees in more than 60 countries, the organization leverages global synergies and local expertise to shape a sustainable future. The company manages around 12,000 customer projects across all life cycles, from planning through implementation, offering diverse opportunities for professional growth. Each entity within Dorsch Global maintains its agility and entrepreneurial spirit while collaborating across regions to address current and emerging issues. As a subsidiary of RSBG SE, a shareholding company of the RAG-Stiftung, Dorsch Global contributes to the foundation’s long-term, purpose-driven mission. Role Description The Health Safety Environment Engineer is a full-time, on-site role based in Al Salamat. This role is responsible for developing, implementing, and monitoring health, safety, and environmental policies, procedures, and standards across project sites and facilities. The engineer conducts risk assessments, safety inspections, and incident investigations, and ensures compliance with relevant regulations and company guidelines. Daily tasks include preparing HSE reports and documentation, supporting the implementation of corrective and preventive actions, and collaborating with project managers and technical teams to integrate HSE requirements into project planning and execution. The role also includes delivering training and awareness programs, promoting a strong safety culture, and continuously improving HSE performance through data analysis and best practices. Qualifications Strong foundation in Health & Safety and Environment Health and Safety (EHS), with proven experience in implementing HSE frameworks and standards. Knowledge of Occupational Health principles, including risk identification, exposure control, and workplace health programs. Competence in Safety Engineering, including hazard analysis, risk assessment, and the design of preventive and protective measures. Experience in Training related to HSE topics, including developing training materials and delivering sessions to diverse audiences. Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (e.g., Environmental, Civil, Mechanical, Industrial) or a related technical discipline; HSE-specific certifications (e.g., NEBOSH, IOSH, OSHA) are an advantage. Familiarity with local and international HSE regulations, standards, and best practices, preferably in engineering, construction, or infrastructure projects. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and reporting skills, with attention to detail and the ability to interpret HSE data and metrics. Effective communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders and promote a proactive safety culture on site. Ability to work on-site in Al Salamat, collaborate in multidisciplinary teams, and adapt to dynamic project environments.

title: VP/Director of Health Safety, Environmental & Regulatory (HSE&R)
description: TITLE: Vice President / Director of Health Safety, Environmental & Regulatory (HSE&R) Please note: Title and compensation will be assigned commensurate with the candidate’s experience. ABOUT THE COMPANY: W&T Offshore, Inc. (NYSE: WTI) is a thriving, independent oil and natural gas producer operating in the Gulf of America, the second-largest producing basin in the U.S. for nearly four decades. ABOUT OUR EMPLOYEES: We have built a team of talented and collaborative individuals who are committed to cultivating a culture of integrity, honesty, trust, respect, and communication. Our mission is to attract and retain like-minded team members who will grow and prosper within our W&T community. W&T offers a competitive total rewards program designed to provide competitive pay, health and financial benefits, and work-life balance. WORKING LOCATION: Houston Office - 5718 WESTHEIMER RD 7 7057 FULL-TIME/PART-TIME: Full-Time SCHEDULE: Mon -Thurs - 9 hours /Friday - 4 hours (in-office) FLSA STATUS: Salary, Non-Exempt POSITION SUMMARY: Reporting to the COO, The Vice President / Director of Health, Safety, Environment & Regulatory (HSE&R) assumes responsibility for guiding the formulation, execution, administration, and continuous enhancement of the Company's safety and environmental strategies and objectives. This role calls for the delivery of expert guidance in health, safety, environmental and regulatory matters to lead and bolster all levels of the organization’s operations. The VP, HSE&R is hands-on and requires current EHS leadership experience (policies and procedures, processes, system implementations, ESG reporting, compliance, regulatory) specific to the regulatory requirements of the offshore oil and gas industry and a publicly traded company. The role is office-based Mon-Thurs (remote Friday) with up to 15% travel to within the company’s operating area (TX, LA, AL). Primary Responsibilities Manage HSE&R Department, with staff located in Houston (TX), New Iberia (LA), Mobile (AL) and Gulf of America (Offshore). Provide HSE&R leadership to all departments including drilling, completions, operations, production, P&A and construction activities, through leading by example and working constructively with the other department managers and staff. Manage W&T’s regulatory responsibilities for all operations, including preparation and submittal of EPs, DOCDs, permit applications and other filings with BSEE, BOEM and applicable State regulators. Responsible for ESG data collection and reporting. Revise and develop key corporate H&S and environmental policies, programs and procedures and roll them out to all business units and departments through face-to-face and online training. Work with in-house and external attorneys on regulatory enforcement and other legal matters. Represent W&T in Industry groups such as the Offshore Operators Committee and API, and with consortiums such as Clean Gulf Associates and Helix Well Control Group. Manage the company’s HSE compliance programs, including performance tracking and reporting both internally and to regulatory agencies. Track all HSE metrics on a routine basis; develop presentation material for executive management’s use. Direct company HSE/SEMS audits, both internally and externally using contractors and internal compliance technicians. Direct effective incident investigations and review and approve final investigation reports and disseminate the lessons learned. Lead efforts for emergency response training and drills. Continue to implement the computer-based Environmental Management Systems for SEMS and compliance. Manage W&T’s drug testing program. Manage the company’s contractor management program, with ISNetworld and internal processes. Manage and direct W&T’s SEMS program for continuous improvement. Manage waste disposal activities to ensure compliance with RCRA, Alabama, Louisiana and Texas waste regulations. Manage all air permitting activities onshore, including the proper installation of pollution control devices and emissions testing and reporting. Also manage all Greenhouse Gas reporting for offshore and onshore. Knowledge, Education & Experience Bachelor of Science degree in Environmental Management, Science, Engineering or equivalent. 15+ years of hands-on Senior HSE management experience and demonstrated track record managing significant HSE programs in the offshore energy sector. Exceptional leadership, organizational and problem-solving skills. Demonstrated quality decision making skills. Highly effective communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to establish excellent working relationships at both the field and management level. Excellent written and oral communication skills. Proven experience communicating and negotiating with government agencies such as BSEE (MMA), BOEM, USCG and State regulators. Knowledge of applicable regulations that are implemented and enforced by BSEE (MMA), BOEM, USCG, OSHA, EPA, PHMSA, AOGB, APSC, ADEM, TRRC and TGLO. Proven experience managing effective SEMS programs. Strong time management, prioritization, and organizational skills Proficiency with all MS Office products (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.) Self-motivated with the ability to adapt work schedule as needed to accomplish objectives. Knowledge of SempCheck or similar computer-based EMS systems Safety or environmental certification, such as CSP is a plus. Physical Requirements Ability to travel offshore as needed via helicopter and/or boat. Ability to pass all required safety training for offshore travel/work. Requires prolonged sitting, some bending and stooping. Occasional lifting up to 10 pounds. Manual dexterity sufficient to operate a computer keyboard and calculator. title: Chief Information Security Officer
description: Position Summary The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) owns enterprise security strategy, risk management, and compliance for the FAL Group of companies under Fortive (Accruent, Gordian, and ServiceChannel) all of which are SaaS / data platform companies in the Facilities and Asset Lifecycle space. This is a senior management role reporting directly to Chief Digital and Services Officer at Accruent, with regular visibility and dotted line reporting accountability to the executive teams at all three operating companies as well as security and IT leadership at Fortive. The CISO is accountable for protecting customer data, enabling enterprise sales through compliance readiness, and building a security program that scales with the company’s growth trajectory through operating company specific security strategy and program management aligned with Fortive’s baseline posture and policy, but extended to meet the needs of each individual operating company. This role sits at the intersection of technical security leadership and business strategy. The successful candidate will be equally comfortable running an incident response, presenting risk posture to the executive teams, and walking an enterprise prospect’s security team through the company’s controls during the sales cycle. The successful candidate will also be a seasoned communicator across, upstream to the executive teams and downstream to the business with a clear track record of calibrating communication (written, verbal, and in-person) appropriately to ensure success of the overall security program. Key Responsibilities Security Strategy & Program Leadership Own and continuously evolve the company’s information security strategy, aligned to business objectives. Take existing security in excellence practices, communities, executive constructs, and awareness/culture programs and continue to grow them and integrate them as part of the larger security strategy. Lead and develop a high-performing security organization spanning security operations, vulnerability and threat management, security engineering, governance/risk/compliance (GRC), application security, AI security, and all associated cyber or cyber adjacent incident response. Set and manage the security budget, including build-vs-buy decisions on tooling and managed services. Ensure the team is budgeted appropriately to meet, interact, grow, develop, and build connections in security across the operating companies, Fortive, and the local security communities they serve. Establish security architecture standards across cloud infrastructure, AI, application development, and data platforms. Be the consistent voice for security across the three businesses translating asks from Fortive (parent company), calibrating messaging from Fortive to the three executive teams, owning messaging from the operating company back to Fortive, and insulating the operating companies from business impact wherever possible. Maintain clear visibility of security posture and strategic programs to the three executive teams, owning cyber considerations for enterprise risk management initiatives, and self-attesting risk assessment initiatives. Chair and lead the Information Security Council (ISC) at each operating company, raising security awareness, calibrating updates, and driving resolution of critical cyber risk through executive collaboration and partnership. Compliance & Certifications Own the company’s compliance posture across SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, Cyber Essentials Plus, CMMC, ISO 42001, and applicable frameworks (HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA, SOX as relevant to the customer base and internal requirements). Lead audit cycles end-to-end — evidence collection, auditor relationships, remediation tracking, and timely certification renewal, while streamlining these operations to minimize business impact. Maintain a current risk register and ensure control gaps are tracked to closure with assigned owners and deadlines and appropriately lead executive risk management escalations with the information security councils at each operating company. Customer Trust & Revenue Enablement Serve as the executive owner of the security review process for enterprise sales — including security questionnaires, customer audits, and contractual security terms. Partner with Sales and Legal to reduce security-related sales cycle friction, treating security posture as a competitive differentiator rather than a cost center. Represent the company in customer-facing security discussions, including Executive Briefing Center engagements with strategic prospects. Risk Management & Incident Response Own the enterprise risk management program, including third-party / vendor risk assessment for the company’s supply chain and subprocessors. Build and maintain the incident response plan; lead the response to any security incident, including coordination with Legal, Communications, and executive leadership. Conduct regular tabletop exercises and ensure the organization is prepared for both technical and reputational dimensions of a security event. Lead regular response tests, tabletops, and resiliency exercises with key business areas and the executive teams at all three operating companies. Governance & Parent Company Reporting Present security posture, risk trends, and program maturity to the Fortive security team and Fortive CISO on a monthly basis. Serve as a key stakeholder in technical and security diligence processes, including those associated with financing events or M&A. Advise the executive team on emerging threats, regulatory changes, and their business implications. Required Qualifications 10+ years in information security, with 5+ years in a senior leadership role (CISO, VP Security, Director of Security or equivalent) at a SaaS or data-intensive company. Demonstrated ownership of SOC 2 and/or ISO 27001 programs, including direct experience managing audit cycles to successful certification. Experience managing executive stakeholders at multiple lines of business at the same time, and nuanced understanding of conglomerate/operating company model. Experience presenting to boards, executive teams — able to translate technical risk into business terms. Strong working knowledge of cloud security (AWS, GCP, and Azure), modern application security practices, and data protection regulations relevant to the company’s markets. Track record of building or scaling a security function, including hiring and developing a team. Experience supporting enterprise sales cycles through customer security reviews and questionnaires. Track record of driving security culture, awareness, trust, and delivering on promises on time with quality across executive teams, and at an employee level. Preferred Qualifications Prior experience leading security at an operating company in a conglomerate/operating company model. Strong track record of maintaining best in class team engagement, retention, growth and development of team and in driving enterprise-wide trust around security. Relevant certifications: CISSP, CISM, or equivalent. Experience with CMMC, FedRAMP, HIPAA, GDPR, or other regulatory frameworks. Fortive Corporation Overview Fortive's essential technology makes the world safer and more productive. We accelerate transformation in high-impact fields like workplace safety, build environments, and healthcare. We are a global industrial technology innovator with a startup spirit. title: Vice President, Global Environmental, Health, and Safety
description: TPI Composites, a trusted, long-term manufacturing partner to the global wind energy market, provides high-quality, cost-effective composite wind blades backed by advanced manufacturing capabilities and our proprietary, AI driven BladeAssure™ validation platform. TPI is headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, operates factories in the U.S. and Mexico and has an engineering development center in Denmark with global service operations in the U.S., Mexico, and EU. Job Description Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Vice President, Environmental Health, Safety and Sustainability provides strategic direction and leadership for TPI’s environmental, health & safety programs. The incumbent is responsible for the continuous development and effective implementation of Safety Policies and Procedures. In addition, the incumbent leads the company’s sustainability program. He/she leads a team of safety professionals to drive and ensure a proactive safety culture across the organization as well as best in class sustainability practices. Key stakeholders include regional business leaders, customers as well as the Senior Leadership team at TPI Responsibilities & Accountabilities Drive a proactive safety culture across the organization Design, implement, and continuously improve enterprise-wide environmental, health & safety strategy and programs consistent with industry best practices, Define short and long term objectives to achieve company safety and sustainability goals and implement KPI’s, monthly reporting and business reviews to communicate progress Assess and drive implementation of optimal health & safety organizational structure, tools, training, programs, governance, and accountability models Leads efforts of safety organization through matrix leadership Provide technical expertise and thought leadership, create synergies and leverage knowledge, personnel, best practices, and resources across the organization Support the company’s US Worker’s Compensation Program effectively. This includes a focus on effective case management, return-to-work programs, and similar relative to work related illness and injuries. Ensure compliance with all environmental, health, and safety standards Monitor and facilitate the progress of environmental sustainability programs and governance systems, consistent with strategies, goals, measurements and reporting standards Lead the organization to behave with a sense of urgency, ensure that it is aligned and attracts the best talent Coordinate the executive level engagement between regions, customers and senior stakeholders Leverage synergies across various sites and participates/leads in sharing best practices Coach and mentor supply chain professionals across the organization Create and promote a culture of collaboration, team-work and fun while delivering to or exceeding expectations Who we are looking for: Minimum Education and Experience Bachelor's Engineering Degree in risk management, industrial Safety and Health, Safety engineering, Safety management, or closely related field 10-15 years’ leadership experience in regional or global manufacturing environment Knowledge and expertise in safety requirements in international locations (Americas and Europe) Proven ability to lead diverse safety teams to achieve organizational objectives Experience in the interpretation and enactment of Safety standards in OSHA and other global regulations Demonstrated ability to establish, implement, and manage best practice environmental, health & safety programs Familiarity with ISO 9001/14001/18001 implementation and program sustainability Ability to lead in a matrix environment Highly developed interpersonal communication skills with the ability to effectively, persuasively, and tactfully interact with employees at all levels of the organization. Highly effective presentation and training delivery skills Demonstrated ability to quickly establish credibility and lead by influence across all levels of the organization, from senior leadership to individual contributors This is a remote, U.S.-based role with willingness and ability to travel internationally to manufacturing sites. Build an effective team committed to organizational goals; foster collaboration among team members. Solution oriented, proactive approach and attitude in resolving issues without compromising quality Strong leadership, mentoring, organizational and communication skills Required Skills and Education - 15+ Years Management/Supervision Experience - Leadership experience in global manufacturing operations required Preferred Skills and Education -Experience in global organization -Experience leading teams through impact/influence -Experience in large scale industrial manufacturing
